subject: FinPay POC scoping — model-fit recommendations & parity acceptance
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: FinPay POC scoping — model-fit recommendations & parity acceptance

Hi Ellen —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

1) Goal: Measure whether an open-model ensemble can meet FinPay's production quality bar vs your current proprietary baseline for transaction categorization and customer reply synthesis. Primary metrics: top-1 classification accuracy (dev set), F1 on the disputed bucket, and a human-rated coherence/accuracy score for synthesized replies (1–5). 

2) Recommended models to trial (initial phase):
- open-llama-34b-q4 (quantized) — cost-efficient baseline for throughput tests
- oasis-large-7b-chat — stronger instruction-following on short contexts
- redwood-curie-pt-7b (our tuned community variant) — middle ground, often matches proprietary baselines on customer phrasing

3) Acceptance thresholds (provisional, we can refine after you share a labeled holdout):
- Top-1 accuracy >= 92% of your proprietary baseline on the classification task
- F1 (disputed) within 0.04 absolute points of baseline
- Human-rated reply score not more than 0.3 points below baseline mean on a 1–5 scale

4) Eval artifacts we'll provide before POC: prompt set (attached), benchmark CSV with recent open-model runs (attached), and the evaluation harness links (Drive). We'll run a no-fine-tune comparison first; if parity gaps are > acceptance, we propose a 2-week instruction-tuning pass on a small labeled corpus.

5) Proposed POC timeline:
- Week 0: NDA/Security QA & sample data exchange
- Week 1: Baseline runs (open models) + initial benchmark report
- Week 2: Optional lightweight tuning + re-eval
- Week 3: Quality review + rollout plan (canary parameters, latency/cost targets)

Next steps for you: share the labeled holdout (anonymized) and the security questionnaire. Once we have those, Marissa will run the baseline jobs and share numbers within 3 business days.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments referenced: redwood-eval-promptset_v1.jsonl (prompt templates and sampling instructions), benchmarks_open_vs_baseline_20261114.csv (pre-run comparisons)

From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finpay.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@finpay.com
Date: 2026-11-15T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinPay POC scoping — model-fit recommendations & parity acceptance

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful and close to what we discussed. A few clarifications from my side: 

- The baseline numbers I referenced on the call are from our in-house model (v2026.08). I can share aggregated stats but not the model artifacts. We'll provide a labeled holdout (~3k rows) and a small unlabeled sample for latency/cost testing.

- Security: attaching our completed Security QA (FinPay_Security_QA_20261115.pdf). Procurement looped in. They will want the standard SOC2 + encryption-at-rest confirmation and a short runbook for data deletion in the POC.

- Acceptance thresholds: the team is most sensitive to false positives in the disputed bucket. Can you confirm whether Redwood can include an audit trail (per-request inputs, prediction probabilities) for every evaluated request?

Happy to proceed on the timeline you suggested. Please confirm the per-token cost we should expect for the open-llama-34b-q4 run (ballpark) and whether we can set a hard cap for the POC spend.

—Ellen
Ellen Park
Director, Automation & AI — FinPay
ellen.park@finpay.com

Attachment: FinPay_Security_QA_20261115.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen.park@finpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinPay POC scoping — model-fit recommendations & parity acceptance

Thanks, Ellen — got the QA doc (thanks for sending). Short answers: 

- Audit trail: yes — Redwood will provide per-request inputs, top-k probabilities (when available), model version, and inference latency in the evaluation logs. We'll redact any PII automatically per your mask rules.

- Cost: rough estimate for open-llama-34b-q4 in our hosted environment is ~$0.008/token for generation-heavy runs; for classification-only (short context) expect ~40–60% lower. For POC we can set a spend cap and throttle jobs; suggest a $2,500 cap to run the full 3k holdout + sampling. If you prefer, we can also run the baseline evaluation on your data in your VPC via Redwood Private to avoid egress — cost is similar but requires a short provisioning window.

- We'll include the benchmark CSV we ran internally (benchmarks_open_vs_baseline_20261114.csv) with per-metric breakdown and the prompt set (attached).

Operational note: for the disputed bucket, we recommend adding a binary abstain rule in the evaluator (i.e., model returns "needs human review" if confidence < threshold). That will let us tune precision/recall trade-offs and evaluate operational cost of manual review.

I'll ask Marissa to schedule the baseline runs once you confirm the data share method (S3 link vs VPC transfer) and the spend cap.

Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-11-16T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: FinPay POC scoping — model-fit recommendations & parity acceptance

Hi Ellen — looping in details from the evaluation team. A few practical items before we start runs: 

- Dataset format: prefer newline-delimited JSONL with fields: id, text, label (if available), metadata. Sample row included in the attached promptset file.

- Holdout split: we'll use your submitted 3k as the labeled holdout for accuracy/F1 and pull a separate 1k for human review scoring to avoid label leakage.

- Benchmarks: the attached CSV includes token-level cost estimates and latency percentiles (p50/p95). We'll run open-llama-34b-q4, oasis-large-7b-chat, and redwood-curie-pt-7b. If we see a consistent gap > acceptance thresholds, we'll propose a 10–14 day instruction-tune using 2–5k examples (you retain all IP).

- Scheduler: To honor your spend cap, we'll run the classification (cheap path) first, then run a small sample of generation-based reply synthesis to estimate human-rated scores. That should fit the $2.5k cap. If you want a hard stop at $1.5k instead, confirm and we'll adjust sampling.

I'll queue the baseline jobs as soon as you provide the S3 link and confirm spend cap.

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Procurement confirmed the $2,500 cap for now and prefers S3 transfer (we'll send a pre-signed link by EOD). A couple of final asks: 

- Please include an explicit definition for the human-rated score rubric (we want consistency across reviewers).
- For the audit trail, procurement asks that logs be retained for 90 days and that deletion instructions are documented for the POC.

If you can send the final runbook and rubric today, we'll approve and upload the holdout. Looking forward to the baseline numbers.

—Ellen
